name: Greece
summary_text: Greece is a workable destination with a clear law-versus-practice gap. The legal framework is among Europe's strongest — it ranks 7th on the ILGA-Europe Rainbow Map, has banned conversion therapy and intersex infant surgery, has a hate-crime law covering gender identity, and legalised same-sex marriage in 2024 (the first Orthodox-majority country to do so). There are no trans-specific border or bathroom restrictions, and the government is progressive with an improving trajectory. But the social reality lags the law. A mob of about 150 people assaulted two trans people in Thessaloniki; an European Court of Human Rights case documented police detention and mistreatment of trans sex workers; surveys show Greeks are markedly more avoidant of public LGBTI visibility than the EU average (63% avoid holding hands); and the UK Foreign Office has issued an LGBTQ travel warning for Greece. Major tourist destinations — Mykonos, Athens's Gazi district, Thessaloniki — are welcoming; outside them the climate is rougher than the law suggests.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on Greece: the marriage-equality law (5089/2024) added SOGIESC equal-treatment guarantees in goods/services, education, healthcare and housing; in March a mob of ~150 attacked two trans people in Thessaloniki (21 arrested, 11 minors), followed by a masked attack on counter-protesters; the Orthodox Church officially opposed marriage equality; transphobic comments targeted Eurovision contestants; 'Family Pride' counter-demonstrations were organised.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (covering 2025) chapter on Greece: the ECtHR condemned Greece for the treatment of an LGBTI Iranian refugee detained pending deportation (Article 3 violation); a criminal case was opened over an online post inciting discrimination against immigrants and LGBTI people; in July the Crete Court of Appeal convicted three French tourists for a 2017 attack.

sources.title: Electra Leda Koutra and Anastasia Katzaki v. Greece
sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe case-law page on Koutra and Katzaki v. Greece (ECtHR app. 459/16, 2017): detention and mistreatment of transgender sex workers and their lawyer by Greek police in 2013 - police stops of trans people on the street and removal from cars; complaints against officers were discontinued; third-party intervention by ILGA-Europe, TGEU, Greek Transgender Support Association and ICRSE.

sources.title: Foreign Office's new travel warning to LGBTQ+ holidaymakers
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (April 2024): the UK Foreign Office updated its Greece travel advice for LGBTQ+ holidaymakers - same-sex relations legal, civil unions since 2015, marriage since February 2024 (first Orthodox-majority country), age of consent 15 for all, and transgender people able to change legal gender; travellers advised to remain alert.

EU FRA LGBTIQ survey III country sheet for Greece (2024): 63% avoid holding hands with a same-sex partner (EU-27: 53%); 36% avoid certain locations for fear of assault (EU-27: 29%); 35% are open about being LGBTIQ (EU-27: 51%); 28% felt discriminated at work (EU-27: 19%).

sources.title: Greece | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): Greece ranked 7th in Europe on the 2025 Rainbow Map; conversion practices banned for minors and IGM criminalised (2022); National Strategy for LGBTQI+ Equality; 2023 anti-bullying education law and employment-discrimination ban on SOGI; February 2024 Law 5089/2024 extended equal-treatment grounds (SOGIESC) across social protection, education, healthcare, housing and goods/services, alongside marriage equality.

sources.title: Trans Rights Index & Map 2025: Backsliding outpaces progress – Where Greece stands - The Press Project - Ειδήσεις, Αναλύσεις, Ραδιόφωνο, Τηλεόραση
sources.claim_summary: The Press Project (May 2025): TGEU's Trans Rights Index & Map 2025 shows backsliding outpacing progress across Europe for the first time; Greece meets 21 of 32 indicators - gaps include age restrictions on name changes, no national action plan, and no legal recognition of trans/non-binary parenthood.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Greece - Wikipedia
sources.claim_summary: Wikipedia overview: same-sex marriage legal since 2024; adoption and foster care; discrimination and hate-speech protections; gender identity and expression (self-ID since 2017); conversion therapy; military service; correctional facilities; social conditions including Pride events and homophobic violence.

sources.title: Greeks consider recognising same-sex couples | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (April 2008): Greece's Justice Ministry pledged a working group on the rights of cohabiting gay couples, to 'analyse all aspects of the issue, international practice and the existing domestic legal and social framework'; the government said it would include same-sex unions in upcoming unmarried-couples legislation.
